title: Exhaustive split filtered free complexes are K-projective
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring in universe $u$. Let $P$ and $F_n$ ($n\in\mathbb N$) be cochain complexes of $A$-modules with carriers in $\max(u,v)$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Suppose there are monomorphisms $\iota_n:F_n\to P$ and maps $s_n:F_n\to F_{n+1}$ with $s_n\iota_{n+1}=\iota_n$, $F_0=0$, and every element of each $P^k$ in the image of some $\iota_n^k$. Suppose every $s_n^k$ has an $A$-linear retraction. Suppose for each $n$ the cokernel complex of $s_n$ is a direct sum, indexed by a set in $\max(u,v)$, of complexes concentrated in integer degrees with the rank-one $A$-module $\operatorname{ULift}^{v}A$ in that degree. Then $P$ is K-projective: every chain map $P\to N$ to an acyclic cochain complex of such modules is homotopic to zero.

source.place: Tag 09KM, lemma-property-P-K-projective, applied to A concentrated in degree zero

proof.text: A chain map from a rank-one free module concentrated in degree k to an acyclic N is a cycle of N in degree k. Acyclicity supplies its primitive in degree k-1, giving a null homotopy. On a coproduct choose these primitives on each generator, which defines a homotopy by the coproduct universal property. The same argument works for shifts.

The compatible monomorphisms make each step monic. Its degreewise retractions and the cokernel exact sequence give a degreewise split short exact sequence F_n to F_(n+1) to its quotient. Its homotopy-category triangle and exact Hom sequence show that if F_n and the quotient have no maps to any shifts of acyclic N, the same holds for F_(n+1). Induction starts with F_0 zero. Thus every finite stage and its shifts are left orthogonal to acyclic complexes.

On the direct sum of F_n form a=identity-successor and b induced by iota_n. In each degree a is injective by inspecting components from index zero upward; b is surjective by exhaustion. A finite tuple in ker(b) can be moved modulo im(a) into a single sufficiently large stage; monicity of its inclusion makes that last component zero. Hence ker(b)=im(a). Choose retractions r_n of each step and compose to get r_(j,i):F_j to F_i. On the j-th summand define a left inverse to a with components -r_(j,0),...,-r_(j,j-1),0,...; composing with identity-successor cancels the earlier components and gives the identity in component j. Consequently the telescope sequence is degreewise split.

The degreewise split telescope sequence yields a distinguished triangle in K(A). Maps from either direct sum to an acyclic complex or its shifts are families of zero maps, by the finite-stage result. The exact Hom sequence therefore makes every map from P to an acyclic complex zero in K(A). The homotopy quotient identifies this with a null homotopy of every chain map, which is precisely IsKProjective.

lean.statement:
theorem isKProjective_of_filtered_free {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) ℤ)
    (F : ℕ → CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) ℤ)
    (ι : ∀ n, F n ⟶ P) (step : ∀ n, F n ⟶ F (n + 1))
    (hzero : IsZero (F 0)) (hmono : ∀ n, Mono (ι n))
    (hcompat : ∀ n, step n ≫ ι (n + 1) = ι n)
    (hexhaustive : ∀ (k : ℤ) (x : P.X k),
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (y : (F n).X k), (ι n).f k y = x)
    (hsplit : ∀ (n : ℕ) (k : ℤ),
      ∃ r : (F (n + 1)).X k ⟶ (F n).X k,
        (step n).f k ≫ r = 𝟙 ((F n).X k))
    (hquot : ∀ n, ∃ (I : Type (max u v)) (degree : I → ℤ),
      Nonempty (cokernel (step n) ≅
        ∐ (fun i : I ↦
          (HomologicalComplex.single (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) (.up ℤ) (degree i)).obj
            (ModuleCat.of A (ULift.{v} A))))) :
    P.IsKProjective
